          A:<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

          Bad breath (halitosis) can be an unpleasant and embarrassing condition.\u00a0 Many of us may not realize that we have bad breath, but everyone has it from time to time, especially in the morning.<\/p>

          There are various reasons one may have bad breath, but in healthy people, the major reason is due to microbial deposits on the tongue, especially the back of the tongue.\u00a0 Some studies have shown that simply brushing the tongue reduced bad breath by as much as 70 percent.<\/p>

          What may cause bad breath?<\/i><\/b><\/p>

          • Morning time<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Saliva flow almost stops during sleep and its reduced cleansing action allows bacteria to grow, causing bad breath.<\/div><\/li>
          • Certain foods<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Garlic, onions, etc.\u00a0 Foods containing odor-causing compounds enter the blood stream; they are transferred to the lungs, where they are exhaled.<\/div><\/li>
          • Poor oral hygiene habits<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Food particles remaining in the mouth promote bacterial growth.<\/div><\/li>
          • Periodontal (gum) disease<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Colonies of bacteria and food debris residing under inflamed gums.<\/div><\/li>
          • Dental cavities and improperly fitted dental appliances<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 May also contribute to bad breath.<\/i><\/b><\/div><\/li>
          • Dry mouth (Xerostomia)<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 May be caused by certain medications, salivary gland problems, or continuous mouth breathing.<\/div><\/li>
          • Tobacco products<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Dry the mouth, causing bad breath.<\/div><\/li>
          • Dieting<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Certain chemicals called ketones are released in the breath as the body burns fat.<\/div><\/li>
          • Dehydration, hunger, and missed meals<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Drinking water and chewing food increases saliva flow and washes bacteria away.<\/div><\/li>
          • Certain medical conditions and illnesses<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Diabetes, liver and kidney problems, chronic sinus infections, bronchitis, and pneumonia are several conditions that may contribute to bad breath.

            <\/div><\/li><\/ul>

            Keeping a record of what you eat may help identify the cause of bad breath. \u00a0Also, review your current medications, recent surgeries, or illnesses with you dentist.<\/b><\/i><\/p>

            \u00a0<\/p>

            What can I do to prevent bad breath?<\/i><\/b><\/p>

            \u00a0<\/p>

            • Practice good oral hygiene<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Brush at least twice a day with an ADA approved fluoride toothpaste and toothbrush.\u00a0 Floss daily to remove food debris and plaque from in between the teeth and under the gumline.\u00a0 Brush or use a tongue scraper to clean the tongue and reach the back areas.\u00a0 Replace your toothbrush every 2 to 3 months.\u00a0 If you wear dentures or removable bridges, clean them thoroughly and place them back in your mouth in the morning.<\/div><\/li>
            • See your dentist regularly<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Get a check-up and cleaning at least twice a year.\u00a0 If you have or have had periodontal disease, your dentist will recommend more frequent visits.<\/div><\/li>
            • Stop smoking\/chewing tobacco<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Ask your dentist what they recommend to help break the habit.<\/div><\/li>
            • Drink water frequently<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Water will help keep your mouth moist and wash away bacteria.<\/div><\/li>
            • Use mouthwash\/rinses<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Some over-the-counter products only provide a temporary solution to mask unpleasant mouth odor.\u00a0 Ask your dentist about\u00a0antiseptic rinses<\/i>\u00a0that not only alleviate bad breath, but also kill the germs that cause the problem.

              <\/div><\/li><\/ul>

              In most cases, your dentist can treat the cause of bad breath.\u00a0 If it is determined that your mouth is healthy, but bad breath is persistent, your dentist may refer you to your physician to determine the cause of the odor and an appropriate treatment plan.<\/p>"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":true,"isLocked":true},{"id":"0768dc9","elType":"container","settings":{"_title":"item #2","content_width":"full","hover_parallax":[{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":30},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":40},"_id":"4ec46ba"},{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":60},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":20},"_id":"e0ee6dc"}]},"elements":[{"id":"aee6335","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

              A:<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

              Brushing and flossing help control the plaque and bacteria that cause dental disease.<\/p>

              Plaque is a film of food debris, bacteria, and saliva that sticks to the teeth and gums.\u00a0 The bacteria in plaque convert certain food particles into acids that cause tooth decay.\u00a0 Also, if plaque is not removed, it turns into calculus (tartar).\u00a0 If plaque and calculus are not removed, they begin to destroy the gums and bone, causing periodontal (gum) disease.<\/p>

              Plaque formation and growth is continuous and can only be controlled by regular brushing, flossing, and the use of other dental aids.<\/p>

              Toothbrushing<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Brush your teeth\u00a0at least twice a day<\/i><\/b>\u00a0(especially before going to bed at night) with an ADA approved soft bristle brush and toothpaste.<\/p>

              • Brush at a 45 degree angle to the gums, gently using a small, circular motion, ensuring that you\u00a0always<\/i>\u00a0feel the bristles\u00a0on the gums<\/i>.<\/div><\/li>
              • Brush the outer, inner, and biting surfaces of each tooth.<\/div><\/li>
              • Use the tip of the brush head to clean the inside front teeth.<\/div><\/li>
              • Brush your tongue to remove bacteria and freshen your breath.<\/div><\/li><\/ul>

                Electric toothbrushes are also recommended.\u00a0 They are easy to use and can remove plaque efficiently.\u00a0 Simply place the bristles of the electric brush on your gums and teeth and allow the brush to do its job, several teeth at a time.<\/b><\/p>

                Flossing<\/b>\u00a0\u2013\u00a0Daily flossing<\/b><\/i>\u00a0is the best way to clean between the teeth and under the gumline.\u00a0 Flossing not only helps clean these spaces, it disrupts plaque colonies from building up, preventing damage to the gums, teeth, and bone.<\/p>

                • Take 12-16 inches (30-40cm) of dental floss and wrap it around your middle fingers, leaving about 2 inches (5cm) of floss between the hands.<\/div><\/li>
                • Using your thumbs and forefingers to guide the floss, gently insert the floss between teeth using a sawing motion.<\/div><\/li>
                • Curve the floss into a \u201cC\u201d shape around each tooth and under the gumline.\u00a0 Gently move the floss up and down, cleaning the side of each tooth.<\/div><\/li><\/ul>

                  Floss holders are recommended if you have difficulty using conventional floss.<\/p>

                  Rinsing<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 It is important to rinse your mouth with water after brushing, and also after meals if you are unable to brush.\u00a0 If you are using an over-the-counter product for rinsing, it\u2019s a good idea to consult with your dentist or dental hygienist on its appropriateness for you.<\/p>"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":true,"isLocked":true},{"id":"5470913","elType":"container","settings":{"_title":"item #3","content_width":"full","hover_parallax":[{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":30},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":40},"_id":"9ca6006"},{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":60},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":20},"_id":"35ca649"}]},"elements":[{"id":"4e95882","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

                  A:<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

                  Over the years there has been some concern as to the safety of amalgam (silver) fillings.\u00a0 An amalgam is a blend of copper, silver, tin and zinc, bound by elemental mercury.\u00a0 Dentists have used this blended metal to fill teeth for more than 100 years.\u00a0 The controversy is due to claims that the exposure to the vapor and minute particles from the mercury can cause a variety of health problems.<\/p>

                  According to the American Dental Association (ADA), up to 76% of dentists use silver containing mercury to fill teeth.\u00a0 The ADA also states that silver fillings are safe and that studies have failed to find any link between silver containing mercury and any medical disorder.<\/p>

                  The general consensus is that amalgam (silver) fillings are safe.\u00a0 Along with the ADA\u2019s position, the Center for Disease Control (CDC), the World Health Organization, the FDA, and others support the use of silver fillings as safe, durable, and cost effective.\u00a0 The U.S. Public Health Service says that the only reason not to use silver fillings is when a patient has an allergy to any component of this type of filling.\u00a0 The ADA has had fewer than 100 reported incidents of an allergy to components of silver fillings, and this is out of countless millions of silver fillings over the decades.<\/p>

                  Although studies indicate that there are no measurable health risks to patients who have silver fillings, we do know that mercury is a toxic material when we are exposed at high, unsafe levels.\u00a0 For instance, we have been warned to limit the consumption of certain types of fish that carry high levels of mercury in them.\u00a0 However, with respect to amalgam fillings, the ADA maintains that when the mercury combines with the other components of the filling, it becomes an inactive substance that is safe.<\/p>

                  There are numerous options to silver fillings, including composite (tooth-colored), porcelain, and gold fillings.\u00a0 We encourage you to discuss these options with your dentist so you can determine which is the best option for you.<\/p>"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":true,"isLocked":true},{"id":"63419da","elType":"container","settings":{"_title":"item #3","content_width":"full","hover_parallax":[{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":30},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":40},"_id":"9ca6006"},{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":60},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":20},"_id":"35ca649"}]},"elements":[{"id":"84e58f0","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

                  A:<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

                  You should have your teeth checked and cleaned\u00a0at least twice a year<\/i><\/b>, though your dentist or dental hygienist may recommend more frequent visits.<\/p>

                  Regular dental exams and cleaning visits are essential in preventing dental problems and maintaining the health of your teeth and gums.\u00a0 At these visits, your teeth are cleaned and checked for cavities. \u00a0Additionally, there are many other things that are checked and monitored to help detect, prevent, and maintain your dental health.\u00a0 These include:<\/p>

                  • Medical history review:\u00a0<\/i><\/b>Knowing the status of any current medical conditions, new medications, and illnesses, gives us insight to your overall health and also your dental health.<\/div><\/li>
                  • Examination of diagnostic x-rays (radiographs):\u00a0<\/i><\/b>Essential for detection of decay, tumors, cysts, and bone loss.\u00a0 X-rays also help determine tooth and root positions.<\/div><\/li>
                  • Oral cancer screening:\u00a0<\/i><\/b>Check the face, neck, lips, tongue, throat, tissues, and gums for any signs of oral cancer.<\/div><\/li>
                  • Gum disease evaluation:\u00a0<\/i><\/b>Check the gums and bone around the teeth for any signs of periodontal disease.<\/div><\/li>
                  • Examination of tooth decay:\u00a0<\/i><\/b>All tooth surfaces will be checked for decay with special dental instruments.<\/div><\/li>
                  • Examination of existing restorations:\u00a0<\/i><\/b>Check current fillings, crowns, etc.<\/div><\/li>
                  • Removal of calculus (tartar)<\/i><\/b>:\u00a0<\/b>Calculus is hardened plaque that has been left on the tooth for sometime and is now firmly attached to the tooth surface.\u00a0 Calculus forms above and below the gum line, and can only be removed with special dental instruments.<\/div><\/li>
                  • Removal of plaque:\u00a0<\/i><\/b>Plaque is a sticky, almost invisible film that forms on the teeth.\u00a0 It is a growing colony of living bacteria, food debris, and saliva.\u00a0 The bacteria produce toxins (poisons) that inflame the gums.\u00a0 This inflammation is the start of periodontal disease!<\/div><\/li>
                  • Teeth polishing<\/strong>:<\/strong><\/em>\u00a0Removes stain and plaque that is not otherwise removed during toothbrushing and scaling.<\/div><\/li>
                  • Oral hygiene recommendations<\/em>:<\/em><\/strong>\u00a0Review and recommend oral hygiene aids as needed (electric dental toothbrushes, special cleaning aids, fluorides, rinses, etc.).<\/div><\/li>
                  • Review dietary habits<\/strong>:<\/strong><\/em>\u00a0Your eating habits play a very important role in your dental health.<\/div><\/li><\/ul>

                    As you can see, a good dental exam and cleaning involves quite a lot more than just checking for cavities and polishing your teeth.\u00a0 We are committed to providing you with the best possible care, and to do so will require regular check-ups and cleanings.<\/p>"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":true,"isLocked":true},{"id":"b1d683a","elType":"container","settings":{"_title":"item #3","content_width":"full","hover_parallax":[{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":30},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":40},"_id":"9ca6006"},{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":60},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":20},"_id":"35ca649"}]},"elements":[{"id":"65a6cff","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

                    A:<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

                    Four out of five people have periodontal disease and don\u2019t know it!\u00a0 Most people are not aware of it because the disease is usually painless in the early stages.\u00a0 Unlike tooth decay, which often causes discomfort, it is possible to have periodontal disease without noticeable symptoms.\u00a0 Having regular dental check-ups and periodontal examinations are very important and will help detect if periodontal problems exist.<\/p>

                    Periodontal disease begins when plaque, a sticky, colorless, film of bacteria, food debris, and saliva, is left on the teeth and gums.\u00a0 The bacteria produce toxins (acids) that inflame the gums and slowly destroy the bone.\u00a0 Brushing and flossing regularly and properly will ensure that plaque is not left behind to do its damage.<\/p>

                    Other than poor oral hygiene, there are several other factors that may increase the risk of developing periodontal disease:<\/p>

                    • Smoking or chewing tobacco<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Tobacco users are more likely than nonusers to form plaque and tartar on their teeth.<\/div><\/li><\/ul>
                      • Certain tooth or appliance conditions<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Bridges that no longer fit properly, crowded teeth, or defective fillings that may trap plaque and bacteria.<\/div><\/li><\/ul>
                        • Many medications<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Steroids, cancer therapy drugs, blood pressure meds, oral contraceptives.\u00a0 Some medications have side affects that reduce saliva, making the mouth dry and plaque easier to adhere to the teeth and gums.<\/div><\/li><\/ul>
                          • Pregnancy, oral contraceptives, and puberty<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Can cause changes in hormone levels, causing gum tissue to become more sensitive to bacteria toxins.<\/div><\/li><\/ul>
                            • Systemic diseases<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Diabetes, blood cell disorders, HIV \/ AIDS, etc.<\/div><\/li><\/ul>
                              • Genetics may play role<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Some patients may be predisposed to a more aggressive type of periodontitis.\u00a0 Patients with a family history of tooth loss should pay particular attention to their gums.<\/div><\/li><\/ul>

                                Signs and Symptoms of Periodontal Disease<\/span><\/b><\/p>

                                • Red and puffy gums<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Gums should never be red or swollen.<\/div><\/li><\/ul>
                                  • Bleeding gums<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Gums should never bleed, even when you brush vigorously or use dental floss.<\/div><\/li><\/ul>
                                    • Persistent bad breath<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Caused by bacteria in the mouth.<\/div><\/li><\/ul>
                                      • New spacing between teeth<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Caused by bone loss.<\/div><\/li><\/ul>
                                        • Loose teeth<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Also caused by bone loss or weakened periodontal fibers (fibers that support the tooth to the bone).<\/div><\/li><\/ul>
                                          • Pus around the teeth and gums<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Sign that there is an infection present.<\/div><\/li><\/ul>
                                            • Receding gums<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Loss of gum around a tooth.<\/div><\/li><\/ul>
                                              • Tenderness or Discomfort<\/b>\u00a0\u2013 Plaque, calculus, and bacteria irritate the gums and teeth.<\/div><\/li><\/ul>

                                                Good oral hygiene, a balanced diet, and regular dental visits can help reduce your risk of developing periodontal disease.<\/p>"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":true,"isLocked":true},{"id":"e47f6e9","elType":"container","settings":{"_title":"Item #6","hover_parallax":[{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":30},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":40},"_id":"ea987a2"},{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":60},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":20},"_id":"1765303"}]},"elements":[{"id":"6132403","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

                                                A:<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

                                                Brushing our teeth removes food particles, plaque, and bacteria from all tooth surfaces,\u00a0except<\/i><\/b>\u00a0in between the teeth.\u00a0 Unfortunately, our toothbrush can\u2019t reach these areas that are highly susceptible to decay and periodontal (gum) disease.<\/p>

                                                Daily flossing is the best way to clean between the teeth and under the gumline.\u00a0 Flossing not only helps clean these spaces, it disrupts plaque colonies from building up, preventing damage to the gums, teeth, and bone.<\/p>

                                                Plaque is a sticky, almost invisible film that forms on the teeth.\u00a0 It is a growing colony of living bacteria, food debris, and saliva.\u00a0 The bacteria produce toxins (acids) that cause cavities and irritate and inflame the gums.\u00a0 Also, when plaque is not removed above and below the gumline, it hardens and turns into calculus (tartar).\u00a0 This will further irritate and inflame the gums and also slowly destroy the bone.\u00a0 This is the beginning of periodontal disease.<\/p>

                                                How to floss properly:<\/b><\/p>

                                                • Take 12-16 inches (30-40cm) of dental floss and wrap it around your middle fingers, leaving about 2 inches (5cm) of floss between the hands.<\/div><\/li>
                                                • Using your thumbs and forefingers to guide the floss, gently insert the floss between teeth using a sawing motion.<\/div><\/li>
                                                • Curve the floss into a \u201cC\u201d shape around each tooth and under the gumline. \u00a0Gently move the floss up and down, cleaning the side of each tooth.<\/div><\/li><\/ul>

                                                  Floss holders are recommended if you have difficulty using conventional floss.<\/p>

                                                  Daily flossing will help you keep a healthy, beautiful smile for life!<\/i><\/p>"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":true,"isLocked":true},{"id":"700993b","elType":"container","settings":{"_title":"Item #7","hover_parallax":[{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":30},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":40},"_id":"9989cea"},{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":60},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":20},"_id":"0521e3d"}]},"elements":[{"id":"9a939e3","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

                                                  A:<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

                                                  If you\u2019re feeling somewhat self-conscious about your teeth, or just want to improve your smile, cosmetic dental treatments may be the answer to a more beautiful, confident smile.<\/p>

                                                  Cosmetic dentistry has become very popular in the last several years, not only due to the many advances in cosmetic dental procedures and materials available today, but also because patients are becoming more and more focused on improving their overall health.\u00a0 This includes dental prevention and having a healthier, whiter, more radiant smile.<\/p>

                                                  There are many cosmetic dental procedures available to improve your teeth and enhance your smile.\u00a0 Depending on your particular needs, cosmetic dental treatments can change your smile dramatically, from restoring a single tooth to having a full mouth make-over.\u00a0 Ask your dentist how you can improve the health and beauty of your smile with cosmetic dentistry.<\/p>

                                                  Cosmetic Procedures:<\/span><\/b><\/p>

                                                  \u00a0<\/p>

                                                  Teeth Whitening:\u00a0<\/b>Bleaching lightens teeth that have been stained or discolored by age, food, drink, and smoking.\u00a0 Teeth darkened as a result of injury or taking certain medications can also be bleached, but the effectiveness depends on the degree of staining present.<\/p>

                                                  Composite (tooth-colored) Fillings:\u00a0<\/b>Also known as \u201cbonding\u201d, composite fillings are now widely used instead of amalgam (silver) fillings to repair teeth with cavities, and also to replace old defective fillings. \u00a0Tooth-colored fillings are also used to repair chipped, broken, or discolored teeth. \u00a0This type of filling is also very useful to fill in gaps and to protect sensitive, exposed root surfaces caused by gum recession.<\/p>

                                                  Porcelain Veneers:\u00a0<\/b>Veneers are thin custom-made, tooth-colored shells that are bonded onto the fronts of teeth to create a beautiful individual smile.\u00a0 They can help restore or camouflage damaged, discolored, poorly shaped, or misaligned teeth.\u00a0 Unlike crowns, veneers require minimal tooth structure to be removed from the surface of the tooth.<\/p>

                                                  Porcelain Crowns (caps):<\/b>\u00a0A\u00a0crown is a tooth-colored, custom-made covering that encases the entire tooth surface restoring it to its original shape and size.\u00a0 Crowns protect and strengthen teeth that cannot be restored with fillings or other types of restorations. \u00a0They are ideal for teeth that have large, fractured or broken fillings and also for those that are badly decayed.<\/p>

                                                  Dental Implants:<\/b>\u00a0Dental implants are artificial roots that are surgically placed into the jaw to replace one or more missing teeth.\u00a0 Porcelain crowns, bridges, and dentures can be made specifically to fit and attach to implants, giving a patient a strong, stable, and durable solution to removable dental appliances.<\/p>

                                                  Orthodontics:\u00a0<\/b>Less visible and more effective brackets and wires are making straightening teeth with orthodontics much more appealing to adult patients. \u00a0Also, in some cases, teeth may be straightened with custom-made, clear, removable aligners that require no braces.<\/p>

                                                  Thanks to the advances in modern dentistry, cosmetic treatments can make a difference in making your smile shine!<\/i><\/p>"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":true,"isLocked":true},{"id":"cf115d9","elType":"container","settings":{"_title":"Item #8","hover_parallax":[{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":30},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":40},"_id":"16c7c3b"},{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":60},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":20},"_id":"01b5bdb"}]},"elements":[{"id":"34ab3cc","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

                                                  A:<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

                                                  Porcelain veneers are very thin shells of tooth-shaped porcelain that are individually crafted to cover the fronts of teeth.\u00a0 They are very durable and will not stain, making them a very popular solution for those seeking to restore or enhance the beauty of their smile.<\/p>

                                                  Veneers may be used to restore or correct the following dental conditions:<\/b><\/p>

                                                  • Severely discolored or stained teeth<\/li>
                                                  • Unwanted or uneven spaces<\/li>
                                                  • Worn or chipped teeth<\/li>
                                                  • Slight tooth crowding<\/li>
                                                  • Misshapen teeth<\/li>
                                                  • Teeth that are too small or large<\/li><\/ul>

                                                    Getting veneers usually requires two visits.\u00a0 Veneers are created from an impression (mold) of your teeth that is then sent to a professional dental laboratory where each veneer is custom-made (for shape and color) for your individual smile.<\/p>

                                                    With little or no anesthesia, teeth are prepared by lightly buffing and shaping the front surface of the teeth to allow for the small thickness of veneers.\u00a0 The veneers are carefully fitted and bonded onto the tooth surface with special bonding cements and occasionally a specialized light may be used to harden and set the bond.<\/p>

                                                    Veneers are an excellent dental treatment that can dramatically improve your teeth and give you a natural, beautiful smile.<\/p>"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":true,"isLocked":true},{"id":"7ff1178","elType":"container","settings":{"_title":"Item #9","hover_parallax":[{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":30},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":40},"_id":"b4aaaae"},{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":60},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":20},"_id":"6d465f4"}]},"elements":[{"id":"a54b00d","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

                                                    A:<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

                                                    Since teeth whitening has now become the\u00a0number one<\/i>\u00a0aesthetic concern of many patients, there are many products and methods available to achieve a brighter smile.<\/p>

                                                    Professional teeth whitening (or bleaching) is a simple, non-invasive dental treatment used to change the color of natural tooth enamel, and is an ideal way to enhance the beauty of your smile.\u00a0 Over-the-counter products are also available, but they are much less effective than professional treatments and may not be approved by the American Dental Association (ADA).<\/p>

                                                    As we age, the outer layer of tooth enamel wears away, eventually revealing a darker or yellow shade.\u00a0 The color of our teeth also comes from the inside of the tooth, which may become darker over time.\u00a0 Smoking, drinking coffee, tea, and wine may also contribute to tooth discoloration, making our teeth yellow and dull.\u00a0 Sometimes, teeth can become discolored from taking certain medications as a child, such as tetracycline.\u00a0 Excessive fluoridation (fluorosis) during tooth development can also cause teeth to become discolored.<\/p>

                                                    It\u2019s important to have your teeth evaluated by your dentist to determine if you\u2019re a good candidate for bleaching.\u00a0 Occasionally, tetracycline and fluorosis stains are difficult to bleach and your dentist may offer other options, such as veneers or crowns to cover up such stains.\u00a0 Since teeth whitening only works on natural tooth enamel, it is also important to evaluate replacement of any old fillings, crowns, etc. before bleaching begins.\u00a0 Once the bleaching is done, your dentist can match the new restorations to the shade of the newly whitened teeth.<\/p>

                                                    Since teeth whitening is not permanent, a touch-up may be needed every several years to keep your smile looking bright.<\/p>

                                                    The most widely used professional teeth whitening systems:<\/b><\/p>

                                                    Home teeth whitening systems:\u00a0<\/b>At-home products usually come in a gel form that is placed in a custom-fitted mouthguard (tray), created from a mold of your teeth.\u00a0 The trays are worn either twice a day for approximately 30 minutes, or overnight while you sleep.\u00a0 It usually takes several weeks to achieve the desired results depending on the degree of staining and the desired level of whitening.<\/p>

                                                    In office teeth whitening:\u00a0<\/b>This treatment is done in the dental office and you will see results immediately.\u00a0 It may require more than one visit, with each visit lasting 30 to 60 minutes.\u00a0 While your gums are protected, a bleaching solution is applied to the teeth.\u00a0 A special light may be used to enhance the action of the agent while the teeth are whitened.<\/p>

                                                    Some patients may experience tooth sensitivity after having their teeth whitened.\u00a0 This sensation is temporary and subsides shortly after you complete the bleaching process, usually within a few days to one weak.<\/p>

                                                    Teeth whitening can be very effective and can give you a brighter, whiter, more confident smile!<\/b><\/p>"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":true,"isLocked":true},{"id":"f7803db","elType":"container","settings":{"_title":"Item #10","hover_parallax":[{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":30},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":40},"_id":"acfc2a3"},{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":60},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":20},"_id":"259402f"}]},"elements":[{"id":"9ba5cba","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

                                                    A:<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

                                                    With many state-of-the-art dental treatments and prevention options available in dentistry today, there are fewer reasons for having to extract (remove) teeth. \u00a0When something does go wrong with a tooth, we try to do everything possible to restore the tooth to its original function. \u00a0Removing a tooth is the last option because we know that removal may lead to severe and costly dental and cosmetic problems if the tooth is not replaced.

                                                    Losing a tooth can be a very traumatic experience and it\u2019s very unfortunate when it does happen.\u00a0 Injury, accident, fracture, severe dental decay, and gum disease are the major reasons for having to remove a tooth.\u00a0 If teeth are lost due to injury or have to be removed, it is imperative that they be replaced to avoid cosmetic and dental problems in the future.

                                                    When a tooth is lost, the jaw bone that helped to support that tooth begins to atrophy, causing the teeth on either side to shift or tip into the open space of the lost tooth.\u00a0 Also, the tooth above or below the open space will start to move towards the open space because there is no opposing tooth to bite on. \u00a0These movements may create problems such as decay, gum disease, excessive wear on certain teeth, and TMJ (jaw joint) problems.\u00a0 These problems and movements do not result immediately, but will eventually appear, compromising your chewing abilities, the health of your bite, and the beauty of your smile.

                                                    Options for replacement of missing teeth:<\/strong><\/span>

                                                    Removable bridges<\/strong>\u00a0- This type of bridge is a good solution for replacing one or more missing teeth, especially in complex dental situations where other replacement options are not possible. They are usually made of tooth-colored, artificial teeth combined with metal clasps that hook onto adjacent natural teeth. Removable bridges are the most economical option for replacing missing teeth, but may be the least aesthetically pleasing. This is because the metal clasps on the appliances are often impossible to completely conceal.

                                                    Fixed bridges<\/strong>\u00a0- This type of bridge is generally made of porcelain or composite material and is anchored (cemented) permanently to a natural teeth adjacent to the missing tooth site. The benefit of this type of bridge is that it is fixed (not removable) and it is very sturdy. The disadvantage is that in order to create a fixed appliance, two healthy, natural teeth will have to be crowned (capped) to hold the bridge in place.

                                                    Dentures<\/strong>\u00a0- This type of tooth replacement is used when most or all of the natural teeth are missing in one dental arch. Dentures are removable artificial teeth that are made to closely resemble the patients\u2019 original teeth.

                                                    Implants<\/strong>\u00a0- Are a great way to replace one or more missing teeth. They may also be great to support ill fitting dentures. A dental implant is an artificial root that is surgically placed into the jaw bone to replace a missing tooth. An artificial tooth is placed on the implant, giving the appearance and feel of a natural tooth. Implants are very stable, durable, and are the most aesthetically pleasing tooth replacement option.

                                                    If you are missing teeth, ask us if they need replacement and what options are available to you. Together we will select the best replacement option for your particular case. Prevention and early treatment is always less involved and less costly than delaying treatment and allowing a serious problem to develop.<\/em><\/p>"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":true,"isLocked":true},{"id":"8c05b25","elType":"container","settings":{"_title":"Item #11","hover_parallax":[{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":30},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":40},"_id":"e02f57d"},{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":60},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":20},"_id":"f690513"}]},"elements":[{"id":"331fee1","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

                                                    A:<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

                                                    Most of us have fillings in our mouths that date back many years and some may have even been placed during our childhood. These fillings may now be old, dark, and unattractive, making us feel self-conscious when we smile, laugh, and talk. Old fillings are not only unattractive, they may also be defective. When a filling is old, the margins (space between the tooth and filling) may eventually open and allow bacteria and food debris to enter, potentially causing dental decay.<\/p>

                                                    Your dentist can check your fillings and evaluate if they are defective and need replacement. Also, if you simply want to replace fillings that are unattractive, you and your dentist can decide which ones should be replaced first and what replacement options would best suit you. There are many state-of-the-art dental filling materials and procedures available today that are quick, painless, and cost effective for replacing old, unattractive or defective fillings.<\/p>

                                                    Options for replacing old, unattractive, or discolored fillings:<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

                                                    Composite (bonding) fillings<\/strong>\u00a0- These are tooth-colored fillings that can be closely matched to the color of your existing teeth. They are particularly well suited for use in front teeth or visible parts of teeth and are one of the best ways to improve the health and beauty of your smile.<\/p>

                                                    Crowns (Caps)<\/strong>\u00a0- These types of restoration are used when a tooth is too damaged and cannot be repaired with a filling or other type of restoration. A crown is a covering that encases the entire tooth surface restoring it to its original shape and size. A crown protects and strengthens the remaining tooth structure and can be made of gold, porcelain, and other tooth-colored materials.<\/p>

                                                    Inlays\/Onlays<\/strong>\u00a0- These restorations are custom made fillings. They can be made of composite resin, porcelain or gold and are made by a dental laboratory and placed by a dentist. Inlays\/onlays are usually best for the posterior chewing surfaces of teeth and are utilized to conservatively repair teeth that have large defective\/unattractive fillings or have been damaged by decay or trauma.<\/p>

                                                    Porcelain veneers<\/strong>\u00a0- Used primarily in the front teeth, veneers are very thin shells of tooth-shaped porcelain that are individually crafted and permanently cemented to the front surface of teeth. They are a great solution for fixing discolored, pitted, shipped, malformed, or slightly crooked teeth. Veneers are also used if you have unwanted spaces. Veneers are very durable, natural looking, and do not stain. This makes veneers a very popular solution for restoring a smile impaired by old, unattractive fillings.<\/p>

                                                    As you can see, there are various options for replacing old, unattractive fillings. These treatments will provide strong, natural, and long-lasting replacement solutions to enhance the health and beauty of your smile.<\/em><\/p>"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":true,"isLocked":true},{"id":"7adda87","elType":"container","settings":{"_title":"Item #12","hover_parallax":[{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":30},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":40},"_id":"58abbd2"},{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":60},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":20},"_id":"e63ac58"}]},"elements":[{"id":"7c621fa","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

                                                    A:<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

                                                    Many people are unaware that having periodontal disease (the destruction of gum tissue and bone that hold our teeth in place) can affect your overall health<\/em>.\u00a0 Periodontal disease is one of the most common infections; often more prevalent than the common cold!\u00a0 Periodontal disease is not only the number one reason people lose teeth; it can also affect the health of your body!<\/p>

                                                    Periodontal disease is a bacterial infection, and in its earliest stages, it\u2019s called gingivitis. \u00a0It starts when an accumulation of plaque (a colony of bacteria, food debris, and saliva) is NOT regularly removed from the gums and teeth.\u00a0 The bacteria in plaque produce toxins\/acids that irritate and infect the gums and eventually destroy the jaw bone that supports the teeth.\u00a0\u00a0When periodontal disease is not treated it can eventually lead to tooth loss!<\/em><\/p>

                                                    There are numerous studies that have looked into the correlation between gum disease and major medical conditions.\u00a0 These studies suggest people with periodontal disease are at a greater risk of systemic disease and indicate that periodontal disease may cause oral bacteria to enter the bloodstream and travel to major organs and begin new infections.\u00a0 Research suggests that periodontal bacteria in the blood stream may:<\/p>

                                                    • Contribute to the development of heart disease<\/div><\/li>
                                                    • Increase the risk of stroke<\/div><\/li>
                                                    • Compromise the health of those that have diabetes or respiratory diseases<\/div><\/li>
                                                    • Increase a woman\u2019s risk of having a preterm, low-birth weight baby<\/div><\/li><\/ul>

                                                      Researchers conclude there is still much research to be done to understand the link between periodontal disease and systemic diseases, but enough research has been done to support that infections in the mouth can play havoc elsewhere in the body.<\/p>

                                                      To ensure a healthy, disease-free mouth, we recommend the importance of regular dental check-ups and cleanings, which include a periodontal evaluation.\u00a0 Also, diligent home care and a proper diet can help reduce the plaque and bacteria in the mouth.<\/p>

                                                      Remember\u2026.the mouth body connection!\u00a0 Taking care of your oral health may contribute to your overall medical health!<\/em><\/p>"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":true,"isLocked":true},{"id":"bb90c96","elType":"container","settings":{"_title":"Item #13","hover_parallax":[{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":30},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":40},"_id":"8ab3afb"},{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":60},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":20},"_id":"c35cd5e"}]},"elements":[{"id":"05e9c8d","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

                                                      A:<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

                                                      Although thorough brushing and flossing remove most food particles and bacteria from easy to reach tooth surfaces, they do not reach the deep grooves on chewing surfaces of teeth. More than 75 percent of dental decay begins in these deep grooves (called pits and fissures). Toothbrush bristles are too large to possibly fit and clean most of these areas. This is where sealants play an important role.<\/p>

                                                      A sealant is a thin plastic coating that covers and protects the chewing surfaces of molars, premolars, and any deep grooves or pits on teeth. Sealant material forms a protective, smooth barrier covering natural depressions and grooves in the teeth, making it much easier to clean and help keep these areas free of decay.<\/p>

                                                      Who may need sealants?<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

                                                      Children and teenagers<\/strong>\u00a0- As soon as the six-year molars (the first permanent back teeth) appear or any time throughout the cavity prone years of 6-16.<\/p>

                                                      Infants<\/strong>\u00a0- Baby teeth are\u00a0occasionally<\/em>\u00a0sealed if the teeth have deep grooves and the child is cavity prone.<\/p>

                                                      Adults<\/strong>\u00a0- Tooth surfaces without decay that have deep grooves or depressions that are difficult to clean.<\/p>

                                                      Sealants are easily applied by your dentist or dental hygienist and the process only takes minutes per tooth. After the chewing surfaces are roughened with an acid solution that helps the sealant adhere to the tooth, the sealant material is \u201cpainted\u201d onto the tooth surface, where it hardens and bonds to the teeth. Sometimes a special light will be used to help the sealant material harden.<\/p>

                                                      After sealant treatment, it\u2019s important to avoid chewing on ice cubes, hard candy, popcorn kernels, or any hard or sticky foods. Your sealants will be checked for wear and chipping at your regular dental check-up.<\/p>

                                                      Combined with good home care, a proper diet, and regular dental check-ups, sealants are very effective in helping prevent tooth decay.<\/em><\/p>"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":true,"isLocked":true},{"id":"7654ebb","elType":"container","settings":{"_title":"Item #14","hover_parallax":[{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":30},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":40},"_id":"033ede3"},{"layer_position_vr":{"unit":"%","size":60},"layer_position_hr":{"unit":"%","size":20},"_id":"024d48e"}]},"elements":[{"id":"d05215f","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

                                                      A:<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

                                                      We\u2019re all at risk for having a tooth knocked out.\u00a0 More than 5 million teeth are knocked out every year!\u00a0 If we know how to handle this emergency situation, we may be able to actually save the tooth.\u00a0 Teeth that are knocked out may be possibly reimplanted if we act quickly, yet calmly, and follow these simple steps:<\/p>

                                                      1. Locate the tooth and handle it only by the crown<\/strong>\u00a0(chewing part of the tooth), NOT by the roots.<\/div><\/li>
                                                      2. DO NOT scrub or use soap or chemicals to clean the tooth.<\/strong>\u00a0 If it has dirt or debris on it, rinse it\u00a0gently<\/em>\u00a0with your own saliva or whole milk.\u00a0 If that is not possible, rinse it\u00a0very gently<\/em>\u00a0with water.<\/div><\/li>
                                                      3. Get to a dentist within 30 minutes.\u00a0<\/strong>\u00a0The longer you wait, the less chance there is for successful reimplantation.<\/div><\/li><\/ol>

                                                        Ways to transport the tooth<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

                                                        • Try to replace the tooth back in its socket immediately. \u00a0Gently bite down on gauze, a wet tea bag or on your own teeth to keep the tooth in place.\u00a0 Apply a cold compress to the mouth for pain and swelling as needed.<\/div><\/li>
                                                        • If the tooth cannot be placed back into the socket, place the tooth in a container and cover with a small amount of your saliva or whole milk.\u00a0 You can also place the tooth under your tongue or between your lower lip and gums.\u00a0 Keep the tooth moist at all times.\u00a0\u00a0Do not transport the tooth in a tissue or cloth.<\/em><\/div><\/li>
                                                        • Consider buying a \u201cSave-A-Tooth\u201d storage container and keeping it as part of your home first aid kit.\u00a0 The kit is available in many pharmacies and contains a travel case and fluid solution for easy tooth transport.<\/div><\/li><\/ul>

                                                          The sooner the tooth is replaced back into the socket, the greater the likelihood it has to survive and possibly last for many years.\u00a0 So be prepared, and remember these simple steps for saving a knocked-out tooth.<\/em><\/p>

                                                          You can prevent broken or knocked-out teeth by:<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

                                                          • Wearing a mouthguard when playing sports<\/div><\/li>
                                                          • Always wearing your seatbelt<\/div><\/li>
                                                          • Avoiding fights<\/div><\/li>
                                                          • Avoid chewing hard items such as ice, popcorn kernels, hard breads, etc.<\/div><\/li><\/ul>"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":true,"isLocked":true}]}],"isInner":true}],"isInner":false}]

Dental Checkups & Cleanings Middletown

Dental Exams & Cleanings

At Chapel Hill Dental Arts, we believe that routine dental exams and cleanings are essential to maintaining a healthy smile and preventing serious oral health problems. Our comprehensive approach ensures that your teeth, gums, and overall oral health are monitored and maintained throughout every stage of life. With the latest dental technology and a team of experienced professionals in Middletown, we provide thorough preventive care to help you stay ahead of potential issues before they become significant concerns.

What to Expect During Your Dental Exam

During your initial dental visit and regular check-ups, our dentist and hygienist will perform a comprehensive exam designed to identify potential concerns early. This allows us to address issues before they require more intensive treatments. Here's what your exam will typically include:

  • Diagnostic X-Rays (Radiographs)

X-rays are an essential tool for detecting hidden issues such as:

  • Tooth decay between teeth or under restorations
  • Bone loss related to gum disease
  • Cysts, tumors, or other abnormalities
  • Root positioning for orthodontic evaluations
  • Oral Cancer Screening

Our team will check your face, neck, lips, tongue, throat, and gums for any signs of oral cancer. Early detection is critical in successfully treating oral cancer, and regular screenings can provide peace of mind.

  • Gum Disease Evaluation - We assess the condition of your gums and supporting bone structure for signs of periodontal disease. Catching gum disease early can prevent further bone loss and keep your teeth securely in place.
  • Examination of Tooth Decay - Using specialized tools, we’ll carefully inspect every tooth surface to identify decay or weakened areas that need treatment. Early detection of cavities can prevent further damage and the need for more invasive procedures.
  • Assessment of Existing Restorations - Our team will check any crowns, fillings, or other dental restorations for signs of wear or damage to ensure they continue to protect your teeth effectively.

What to Expect During a Professional Dental Cleaning

Even if you brush and floss regularly, professional cleanings are essential to maintain healthy teeth and gums. Cleanings are typically performed by one of our Registered Dental Hygienists, who are skilled in removing the buildup that regular brushing can’t eliminate. Here’s what your cleaning appointment will include:
  1. Removal of Calculus (Tartar) - Calculus is hardened plaque that forms when plaque is left on the teeth for an extended period. It can build up both above and below the gumline and cannot be removed through regular brushing or flossing. Our hygienist will use specialized instruments to remove this buildup to prevent further gum irritation and infection.

  2. Removal of Plaque - Plaque is a sticky, bacteria-filled film that continuously forms on your teeth. When not removed, the bacteria in plaque produce toxins that irritate the gums, leading to gingivitis and, eventually, periodontal disease. Professional cleanings target and eliminate plaque in hard-to-reach areas.

  3. Teeth Polishing - Once the plaque and calculus are removed, we’ll polish your teeth to remove stains and give them a smooth, clean surface. Polishing also helps prevent plaque from reattaching to the enamel, keeping your teeth looking their best.

  4. Professional Flossing and Fluoride Application (Optional) - After polishing, your hygienist may floss between your teeth to ensure all remaining debris is removed. For added protection, fluoride treatments may also be recommended to strengthen your enamel and help prevent cavities.

Why Regular Exams and Cleanings Are Essential

Regular dental exams and cleanings are the cornerstone of preventive dentistry. Here’s why scheduling these visits every six months is critical to your oral health:

  • Prevents gum disease: Professional cleanings remove bacteria that cause gingivitis and periodontal disease, preventing further complications.
  • Detects issues early: Regular exams allow us to catch potential problems—such as cavities or gum disease—before they worsen.
  • Preserves your teeth: By removing plaque and tartar, we help prevent decay and bone loss, keeping your natural teeth healthy for as long as possible.
  • Maintains overall health: Studies have shown links between oral health and conditions such as heart disease and diabetes. Taking care of your mouth can positively impact your general well-being.

How Often Should You Schedule Dental Exams and Cleanings?

We recommend that most patients schedule dental exams and cleanings every six months to maintain optimal oral health. However, patients with specific conditions, such as periodontal disease or those undergoing orthodontic treatment, may need more frequent visits.

Signs You May Be Due for a Dental Exam and Cleaning

If you are experiencing any of the following, it’s time to schedule a visit:

  • Persistent bad breath or a bad taste in your mouth
  • Bleeding gums when brushing or flossing
  • Sensitivity to hot, cold, or sweet foods
  • Pain or swelling in the gums or teeth
  • Stains or buildup on your teeth that regular brushing can’t remove

Book Your Dental Exam and Cleaning Today

Taking care of your teeth and gums doesn’t just give you a beautiful smile—it helps you stay healthy for life. At Chapel Hill Dental Arts, we are committed to providing comprehensive preventive care in a comfortable, relaxing environment.

Don’t wait until problems arise—schedule your next exam and cleaning today! Our team looks forward to helping you maintain a healthy smile for years to come. Call us or use our online appointment request form to book your visit.

At Chapel Hill Dental Arts, we believe that routine dental exams and cleanings are essential to maintaining a healthy smile and preventing serious oral health problems. Our comprehensive approach ensures that your teeth, gums, and overall oral health are monitored and maintained throughout every stage of life. With the latest dental technology and a team of experienced professionals in Middletown, we provide thorough preventive care to help you stay ahead of potential issues before they become significant concerns.

During your initial dental visit and regular check-ups, our dentist and hygienist will perform a comprehensive exam designed to identify potential concerns early. This allows us to address issues before they require more intensive treatments. Here's what your exam will typically include:

  • Diagnostic X-Rays (Radiographs)

X-rays are an essential tool for detecting hidden issues such as:

  • Tooth decay between teeth or under restorations
  • Bone loss related to gum disease
  • Cysts, tumors, or other abnormalities
  • Root positioning for orthodontic evaluations
  • Oral Cancer Screening

Our team will check your face, neck, lips, tongue, throat, and gums for any signs of oral cancer. Early detection is critical in successfully treating oral cancer, and regular screenings can provide peace of mind.

  • Gum Disease Evaluation - We assess the condition of your gums and supporting bone structure for signs of periodontal disease. Catching gum disease early can prevent further bone loss and keep your teeth securely in place.
  • Examination of Tooth Decay - Using specialized tools, we’ll carefully inspect every tooth surface to identify decay or weakened areas that need treatment. Early detection of cavities can prevent further damage and the need for more invasive procedures.
  • Assessment of Existing Restorations - Our team will check any crowns, fillings, or other dental restorations for signs of wear or damage to ensure they continue to protect your teeth effectively.

Here’s what your cleaning appointment will include:"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"},{"id":"2e65104","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"
  1. Removal of Calculus (Tartar) - Calculus is hardened plaque that forms when plaque is left on the teeth for an extended period. It can build up both above and below the gumline and cannot be removed through regular brushing or flossing. Our hygienist will use specialized instruments to remove this buildup to prevent further gum irritation and infection.

  2. Removal of Plaque - Plaque is a sticky, bacteria-filled film that continuously forms on your teeth. When not removed, the bacteria in plaque produce toxins that irritate the gums, leading to gingivitis and, eventually, periodontal disease. Professional cleanings target and eliminate plaque in hard-to-reach areas.

  3. Teeth Polishing - Once the plaque and calculus are removed, we’ll polish your teeth to remove stains and give them a smooth, clean surface. Polishing also helps prevent plaque from reattaching to the enamel, keeping your teeth looking their best.

  4. Professional Flossing and Fluoride Application (Optional) - After polishing, your hygienist may floss between your teeth to ensure all remaining debris is removed. For added protection, fluoride treatments may also be recommended to strengthen your enamel and help prevent cavities.
"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"},{"id":"443d425","elType":"widget","settings":{"title":"Why Regular Exams and Cleanings Are Essential ","header_size":"h3","typography_typography":"custom","typography_font_family":"Playfair Display","typography_font_weight":"700","typography_font_style":"normal","__globals__":{"title_color":"globals/colors?id=text"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"heading"},{"id":"cb34128","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

Regular dental exams and cleanings are the cornerstone of preventive dentistry. Here’s why scheduling these visits every six months is critical to your oral health:

  • Prevents gum disease: Professional cleanings remove bacteria that cause gingivitis and periodontal disease, preventing further complications.
  • Detects issues early: Regular exams allow us to catch potential problems—such as cavities or gum disease—before they worsen.
  • Preserves your teeth: By removing plaque and tartar, we help prevent decay and bone loss, keeping your natural teeth healthy for as long as possible.
  • Maintains overall health: Studies have shown links between oral health and conditions such as heart disease and diabetes. Taking care of your mouth can positively impact your general well-being.

If you are experiencing any of the following, it’s time to schedule a visit:

  • Persistent bad breath or a bad taste in your mouth
  • Bleeding gums when brushing or flossing
  • Sensitivity to hot, cold, or sweet foods
  • Pain or swelling in the gums or teeth
  • Stains or buildup on your teeth that regular brushing can’t remove

Taking care of your teeth and gums doesn’t just give you a beautiful smile—it helps you stay healthy for life. At Chapel Hill Dental Arts, we are committed to providing comprehensive preventive care in a comfortable, relaxing environment.

Don’t wait until problems arise—schedule your next exam and cleaning today! Our team looks forward to helping you maintain a healthy smile for years to come. Call us or use our online appointment request form to book your visit.

item.title: Digital Dental X-Rays
item.dc:creator: tntadmin
item.content:encoded:
Digital Dental X-Rays Middletown

Digital radiography (digital x-ray) is the latest technology used to take dental x-rays. This technique uses an electronic sensor (instead of x-ray film) that captures and stores the digital image on a computer. This image can be instantly viewed and enlarged helping the dentist and dental hygienist detect problems easier. Digital x-rays reduce radiation 80-90% compared to the already low exposure of traditional dental x-rays.

Dental x-rays are essential, preventative, diagnostic tools that provide valuable information not visible during a regular dental exam. Dentists and dental hygienists in Middletown use this information to safely and accurately detect hidden dental abnormalities and complete an accurate treatment plan. Without x-rays, problem areas may go undetected.

Dental x-rays may reveal:

  • Abscesses or cysts.
  • Bone loss.
  • Cancerous and non-cancerous tumors.
  • Decay between the teeth.
  • Developmental abnormalities.
  • Poor tooth and root positions.
  • Problems inside a tooth or below the gum line.


Detecting and treating dental problems at an early stage may save you time, money, unnecessary discomfort, and your teeth!

Are dental x-rays safe?

We are all exposed to natural radiation in our environment. Digital x-rays produce a significantly lower level of radiation compared to traditional dental x-rays. Not only are digital x-rays better for the health and safety of the patient, they are faster and more comfortable to take, which reduces your time in the dental office. Also, since the digital image is captured electronically, there is no need to develop the x-rays, thus eliminating the disposal of harmful waste and chemicals into the environment.Even though digital x-rays produce a low level of radiation and are considered very safe, dentists still take necessary precautions to limit the patient’s exposure to radiation. These precautions include only taking those x-rays that are necessary, and using lead apron shields to protect the body.

How often should dental x-rays be taken?

The need for dental x-rays depends on each patient’s individual dental health needs. Your dentist and dental hygienist will recommend necessary x-rays based upon the review of your medical and dental history, a dental exam, signs and symptoms, your age, and risk of disease. A full mouth series of dental x-rays is recommended for new patients. A full series is usually good for three to five years. Bite-wing x-rays (x-rays of top and bottom teeth biting together) are taken at recall (check-up) visits and are recommended once or twice a year to detect new dental problems.[wpr-template id="1079"]

At Chapel Hill Dental Arts in Middletown, we take pride in helping patients achieve beautiful, healthy smiles through personalized cosmetic and restorative treatments. Browse through before-and-after photos of real patient transformations, including veneers, Invisalign®, teeth whitening, and dental implants. 

Each smile tells a story of renewed confidence and enhanced oral health. Let these success stories inspire you to take the next step toward your dream smile!

item.content:encoded:
Chapel Hill Dental Arts Blog

Stay informed and empowered with the latest insights from the Chapel Hill Dental Arts Blog. Here, we share expert tips on oral health, cosmetic dentistry, preventive care, and industry trends to help you maintain a healthy and radiant smile. Whether you’re curious about the benefits of Invisalign® or looking for advice on managing dental anxiety, our blog offers practical information for patients of all ages.Check back regularly for updates and news from our dental team!

Request a Dental Appointment Middletown

Address :

429 Highway 35, Red Bank, NJ 07701

Send Message

Meet Our Doctors

Expert & Experienced

Dr. Asim Zaidi

Doctor of Medicine in Dentistry

Dr. Kristen Blumberger

DMD - Middletown, NJ

Dr. Reff

DDS Specializing in Dental Implants and Teeth In A Day

Meet the Team & Tour the Office

Prosthodontics & Implants in Middletown, NJ

Welcome to Chapel Hill Dental Arts

  • Prosthodontics For An Improved Smile
  • High Standards, Exceptional Results
  • Minutes from Downtown Red Bank
(732) 365-0123 Book an Appointment About Our Practice

Your Trusted Red Bank & Middletown Cosmetic Dentist!

At our Middletown dental practice, we provide all specialties in-house, granting patients a comprehensive and convenient experience. Our dentists, specialists, and professional staff cater to your oral health needs and aesthetic goals. Dr. Asim Zaidi, DMD and the rest of the team at Chapel Hill Dental Arts is dedicated to restoring our patients’ confidence, smile, and function with comprehensive dental treatments.

Recognized for Excellence in Dentistry Book an Appointment

Schedule Your Appointment at our Highly Reviewed Dental Practice

Dr. Zaidi and the team of Chapel Hill Dental Arts are appreciative of receiving over 1000 five star reviews on Google! We value the feedback of our existing patients and encourage new patients to join the Chapel Hill Dental Arts family. Click the badge below to read our reviews. Book an Appointment

Full-Service Dental Care

Comprehensive Dental Services in Red Bank

Our dentists in Middletown offer patients a comprehensive dental experience that allows you to visit just one practice for your many needs. Our dental office is equipped with the latest in dental technology, enhancing our quality dental care and improving the efficiency of your treatment. From basic cleanings and preventive measures to providing full smile makeovers, we have the services you need for a brand new smile.

Cleanings & Prevention

A preventive program involves the patient, dentist, & staff together to prevent dental issues.

01.

Cosmetic Dentistry

For patients seeking cosmetic dental treatment, our team is highly experienced in many restorative procedures.

02.

Restorations

If your teeth need restoration, we’ll discuss options and recommend the most comfortable, least invasive treatment. 03.

Periodontics

Periodontics is a dental specialty focused on preventing, diagnosing, and treating gum and jawbone disease. 04.

In the News

See More Meet Our Doctors

Expert & Experienced

Dr. Asim Zaidi

Doctor of Medicine in Dentistry

Dr. Kristen Blumberger

DMD - Middletown, NJ

Dr. Reff

DDS Specializing in Dental Implants and Teeth In A Day

Meet the Team & Tour the Office

Our skilled hygienists, experienced dental assistants, and friendly coordinators work together to ensure every visit is comfortable, efficient, and tailored to your needs. We look forward to welcoming you and providing exceptional dental care in a friendly, modern environment at our dental office near you.

Take a Tour

item.title: Dental Implant Credit Qualification
item.dc:creator: tntadmin
item.content:encoded:
Restore Your Smile with Dental Implants – Financing Available!

Discover durable, natural-looking solutions for missing teeth. Check your financing options now and start your journey to a healthier, more confident smile.

Pre-Qualify for Financing Estimate Your Monthly Payments

Why Choose Dental Implants?

Missing teeth don't just affect your appearance — they can impact your overall health, bone structure, and confidence. Dental implants in Middletown replace both the root and visible portion of the tooth, preventing bone loss and restoring your bite. At Chapel Hill Dental Arts PA, our specialists offer advanced implant solutions, providing you with a one-stop shop for a strong, beautiful smile.

Benefits of Dental Implants:

  • Look, feel, and function like natural teeth
  • Help preserve bone density
  • Restore bite strength and stability

     

Boost your confidence and oral health!

Financing Made Simple

Easy, Flexible Financing Options

We proudly offer financing through CareCredit to make dental implants more affordable. Pre-qualifying only takes a few minutes and won’t affect your credit score!

Pre-Qualify for Financing Estimate Your Monthly Payments We recommend getting pre-qualified before requesting a consultation to make the process even smoother!Custom Solutions for Your Smile

Your Implant Options

Our implant specialists, Dr. Asim Zaidi and Dr. Steve Reff, will guide you every step of the way, using advanced technology like CT scans for precise, comfortable results.

Single Dental Implants

Perfect for replacing individual missing teeth without impacting neighboring teeth.

01.

Implant-Supported Bridges

A strong, healthy option to replace multiple missing teeth.

02.

Implant-Supported Dentures

Same-day full-arch restoration available, crafted right in our in-house dentures lab.

03.

Expert Care, All Under One Roof

Meet Your Implant Specialists

From consultation to completion, you're in expert hands. Our team includes an oral surgeon and a periodontist specializing in implant dentistry. We also offer nitrous oxide sedation for your comfort and provide comprehensive answers to any questions you may have along the way.

We proudly serve patients in Red Bank, Middletown, Holmdel, and throughout Monmouth County.

Take the First Step Toward Your New Smile

item.title: Dental Crowns
item.dc:creator: tntadmin
item.content:encoded:
Dental Crowns Middletown

A crown (or cap) is a covering that encases the entire tooth surface restoring it to its original shape and size. A crown protects and strengthens tooth structure that cannot be restored with fillings or other types of restorations.

Although there are several types of crowns, porcelain (tooth colored crown) are the most popular, because they resemble your natural teeth. They are highly durable and will last many years, but like most dental restorations, they may eventually need to be replaced. Porcelain crowns in Middletown are made to match the shape, size, and color or your teeth giving you a natural, long-lasting beautiful smile.

Reasons for crowns:

  • Broken or fractured teeth.
  • Cosmetic enhancement.
  • Decayed teeth.
  • Fractured fillings.
  • Large fillings.
  • Tooth has a root canal.

What does getting a crown involve?

A crown procedure usually requires two appointments.  Your first appointment will include taking several highly accurate molds (or impressions) that will be used to create your custom crown.  A mold will also be used to create a temporary crown which will stay on your tooth for approximately two weeks until your new crown is fabricated by a dental laboratory.

While the tooth is numb, the dentist will prepare the tooth by removing any decay and shaping the surface to properly fit the crown.  Once these details are accomplished, your temporary crown will be placed with temporary cement and your bite will be checked to ensure you are biting properly.

At your second appointment your temporary crown will be removed, the tooth will be cleaned, and your new crown will be carefully placed to ensure the spacing and bite are accurate.

You will be given care instructions and encouraged to have regular dental visits to check your new crown.

item.title: Veneers
item.dc:creator: tntadmin
item.content:encoded:
Veneers Middletown

Veneers are very thin pieces of durable, tooth shaped porcelain that are custom made (for shape and color) by a professional dental laboratory. They are bonded onto the front of teeth to create a beautiful and attractive smile.

Veneers in Middletown can completely reshape your teeth and smile. They can often be alternatives to crowns and the ideal solution in treating many dental conditions.

As with most dental restorations, veneers are not permanent and may someday need replacement. They are very durable and will last many years, giving you a beautiful long lasting smile.

Reasons for porcelain veneers:

  • Cosmetically, to create a uniform, white, beautiful smile.
  • Crooked teeth.
  • Misshapen teeth.
  • Severely discolored or stained teeth.
  • Teeth that are too small or large.
  • Unwanted or uneven spaces.
  • Worn or chipped teeth.

What does getting porcelain veneers involve?

Getting veneers usually requires two visits to complete the process, with little or no anesthesia required during the procedure. The teeth are prepared by lightly buffing and shaping the surface to allow for the thickness of the veneer. A mold or impression of the teeth is taken and a shade (color) will then be chosen by you and the dentist. On the second visit the teeth will be cleansed with special liquids to achieve a durable bond. Bonding cement is then placed between the tooth and veneer and a special light beam is used to harden and set the bond. You will receive care instructions for veneers. Proper brushing, flossing and regular dental visits will aid in the life of your new veneers. [wpr-template id="1079"]

Veneers are very thin pieces of durable, tooth shaped porcelain that are custom made (for shape and color) by a professional dental laboratory. They are bonded onto the front of teeth to create a beautiful and attractive smile.

Veneers in Middletown can completely reshape your teeth and smile. They can often be alternatives to crowns and the ideal solution in treating many dental conditions.

As with most dental restorations, veneers are not permanent and may someday need replacement. They are very durable and will last many years, giving you a beautiful long lasting smile.

item.title: Teeth Whitening
item.dc:creator: tntadmin
item.content:encoded:
Teeth Whitening Middletown

Tooth whitening (or bleaching) is a simple, non-invasive dental treatment in Middletown used to change the color of natural tooth enamel and is an ideal way to enhance the beauty of your smile.

Because having whiter teeth has now become the number one aesthetic concern of most patients, there are a number of ways to whiten teeth. The most popular method is using a home tooth whitening system that will whiten teeth dramatically. Since tooth whitening only works on natural tooth enamel, it is important to evaluate replacement of any old fillings, crowns, etc. Replacement of any restorations will be done after bleaching so they will match the newly bleached teeth.

Tooth whitening is not permanent. A touch-up maybe needed every several years, and more often if you smoke, drink coffee, tea, or wine.

Reasons for tooth whitening:

  • Fluorosis (excessive fluoridation during tooth development).
  • Normal wear of outer tooth layer.
  • Stained teeth due to medications (tetracycline, etc.).
  • Yellow, brown stained teeth.

What does tooth whitening involve?

This type of tooth whitening usually requires two visits. At the first appointment, impressions (molds) will be made of your teeth to fabricate custom, clear plastic, trays. At your second appointment, you will try on the trays for proper fit, and adjustments will be made if necessary. The trays are worn with special whitening solution either twice a day for 30 minutes or overnight for a couple of weeks depending on the degree of staining and desired level of whitening. It is normal to experience tooth sensitivity during the time you are whitening your teeth, but it will subside shortly after you have stopped bleaching. You will receive care instructions for your teeth and trays, and be encouraged to visit your dentist regularly to help maintain a beautiful, healthy, white smile.[wpr-template id="1079"]
